experiment: Does activation-weighted scale fitting beat the plain mean-|W| scale for 1-bit experts? Byte cost is IDENTICAL between arms (1 bit/weight + one fp16 scale per group); only the objective the scale is fitted against changes. A pure capability comparison at fixed EBPW.
method: Per-input-channel second moments captured from REAL forward passes by wrapping SwitchLinear.__call__ over 2x512 tokens (78/78 tensors captured, asserted non-empty). Scale becomes the d-weighted mean of |W| over the group, which minimises sum_j d_j (W_ij - s*sign(W_ij))^2.
RESULT_REFUTED: Activation calibration is WORSE on all three pairs: ppl +1.9%, +1.0%, +1.9%, and cosine falls in every case (0.7995->0.7970, 0.8013->0.7991, 0.8163->0.8141). This REFUTES the prediction I recorded one step earlier, that activation-aware binarisation was where the next real information would be. It is not, in this form.
IDENTITY_BROKE_EXACTLY_WHERE_THEORY_SAYS: For the uncalibrated arms magnitude_ratio == direction_similarity to 9 digits. For the calibrated arms they SEPARATE (0.8025 vs 0.7970). The proof only holds for the unweighted mean scale, so this is a second, independent confirmation of that derivation rather than a new anomaly. Note the direction: the weighted scale RAISES the reconstruction norm while LOWERING directional agreement -- it inflates scales in high-activation groups.
WHY_IT_PROBABLY_FAILED_and_what_would_te: The scale is fitted per (expert, output row, group), but d was pooled across every token routed through that SwitchLinear -- shared by all 64 experts. Experts are ROUTED and each sees a different token sub-distribution, so the statistic does not match the parameter it is weighting. The discriminating experiment is PER-EXPERT moments (accumulate d separately per routed expert id), which this harness does not yet collect. Until that is run, the honest claim is narrow: POOLED activation weighting fails. Activation-awareness as such is NOT refuted.
CAVEATS: Calibration set is 2x512 tokens from the same corpus the NLL is scored on; a larger or disjoint set could change the magnitude but is unlikely to flip a consistent 3/3 negative.
Diagonal approximation to E[xx^T]; no cross-channel correlation modelled.
